Decisions from the fourth review, 07-11-2026 (the recommended option of each, taken on the user's instruction).

60. Second person: a second reviewer is named in P.2 before phase 1 (promotion approver, ruleset code-owner approver, co-acceptor of Security findings), and so is the owner of each proof repo. If none is named, the plan pauses at gate A. The names are not known yet and are not invented here. Rejected: a documented solo bypass of the ruleset with an owner-less sample check (it removes the independence that decisions 20, 36 and 56 rely on). Revisit trigger: the second reviewer leaves, and the plan pauses again until another is named.
61. Freshness record: a mutable file on the package repo's default branch, written only by the pin-update workflow with the App token, dates in UTC, stale after 30 days. Rejected: a release at least every 30 days (every consumer would get an upgrade pull request with no content change). Revisit trigger: the file is edited by anything other than the workflow.
62. Drift detection: the plan states that `--check` detects drift only in repos that wire it, and recommends the shared plan's scheduled drift workflow (task 6.4) as the independent detector without making it gate the release. Rejected: a hard dependency on that workflow (governance does not gate the release, decision 23). Revisit trigger: Security asks for independent detection before adoption.
63. Timebox and approvals: the gate A clock starts at the later of P.2 complete and P.4 answered. A P.4 request with no answer after five working days is blocked and escalated to the organisation GitHub administrator, and the wait does not count against the timebox. Amends decision 39. Rejected: starting at P.2 (the box is spent waiting), no escalation rule. Revisit trigger: the first P.4 escalation.
64. CODEOWNERS layout: the pins live in a separate `Pins.pkl` with the second reviewer as code owner and no Security requirement, protected by the pin-update checks, and the release, permissions, token and `.claude/settings.json` builtins are in their own files with Security as code owner. Rejected: one Builtins file with Security on every change (every pin bump would wait two days). Revisit trigger: a pin change causes an incident, then Security joins as code owner of the pins.
65. Known-bad list: fetched and cached like the freshness record, with a snapshot bundled in the runner as fallback, plus a pinned issue in the package repo and a message to the owners as the out-of-band notice. Rejected: bundled only (stale by design), fetched only (an outage hides it). Revisit trigger: the list and the runner disagree during a real incident.
66. Gate B builtin criterion: the slice has 3 builtins, and any one that cannot render semantically equal after one fix attempt abandons the plan. The written estimate for the other 5 builtins abandons it if more than 2 fail (decision 43). Rejected: a flat count of 2 of 8, which is nearly vacuous on a slice of 3. Revisit trigger: owners change the number at P.1.
67. Test releases (0.0.x): releases for the 7.4 tests and the 7.6 benefit test are cut in a throwaway test package repo deleted after phase 7, never in the real package repo, whose version history stays final-numbered. Spike releases stay in the spike repo (decision 51). Rejected: publishing them in the real repo (permanent out-of-order versions in a public package). Revisit trigger: the throwaway repo cannot reproduce the real release pipeline.
68. Owner sign-off silence: an owner who does not sign within five working days, with a reminder at three, blocks the item, and it is escalated to the organisation GitHub administrator. A sign-off is never defaulted, and the proof report records the repo as not signed, so the Done list is unmet for it. Rejected: a default sign-off (weakens decision 56), closing the plan. Revisit trigger: an owner is unreachable for more than two weeks, then the plan owner and the administrator decide whether to drop that repo from the proof.
